sections.title: Method — deterministic (free) NER cross-validation eval
sections.context: NER cross-validation ( ner_cross_validation_enabled , default False ) is a fully deterministic post-LLM pass: it boosts/penalizes annotation confidence using spaCy NER labels vs. a per-ontology branch affinity map, rejecting spans that fall below 0.20. Running the pipeline with llm=None gives a reproducible, /bin/bash ruler→NER→reconcile→resolve path that still exercises the flag. This pack reports that free comparison; the authoritative full-pipeline (LLM-sourced) comparison is spend-gated and queued to the QA portal. sections.title: Result — flag OFF vs ON, precision / recall / F1
sections.context: P R F1 TP FP FN NER off 1.000 1.000 1.000 52 0 0 NER on 1.000 1.000 1.000 52 0 0 delta +0.000 +0.000 +0.000 Recommendation: HOLD_no_f1_gain. On the unambiguous deterministic set NER cross-validation is recall-safe — it was free to reject any of the 52 scored spans and rejected none — but shows no F1 gain there. Its discriminating signal lives in the borderline + LLM-sourced concepts, which the free tier does not cover. Default stays False pending the spend-gated run.

sections.title: Spend estimate — authoritative full-mode run (queued)
sections.context: The authoritative flip signal needs the LLM candidate stages ON. Because the NER flag only changes deterministic reconciliation, that is one LLM pass per doc + a free replay OFF/ON. Token-grounded estimate over the 6 gold docs (google/gemini-3-flash-preview): ~114K input + 43K output tokens → /bin/bash.03–/bin/bash.14 (range = flash-class price assumption, the one figure to confirm). Queued to the QA portal ( briefs/qa/pending-questions.jsonl ) per TODAY policy — not run.
